content:
Jon: heads-up — observed ~1.2k requests in last hour where clients sent X-Redwood-Version: v1 but ended up routed to v2 replicas. Risk: silent behavior change for customers.
Tara: ouch. where is coercion happening? proxy or router?
Jon: looks like the edge proxy has a small header-normalization transform introduced in the november patch. it lowercased and stripped prefix rules and then router matched against canonical v2 tag.
Matt: can you paste the transform logic?
Jon: sure — snippet from the proxy config: ```lua
if req.headers['x-redwood-version'] then
  req.headers['x-redwood-version'] = string.lower(req.headers['x-redwood-version'])
  req.headers['x-redwood-version'] = req.headers['x-redwood-version']:gsub('^version%-','')
end
``` 
Anna: so clients sending "V1" or "version-v1" got coerced -> "v1" -> router matching order picked v2 because of prefix fallthrough? that's surprising.
Tara: router matching prefers latest compatible variant when header equals alias. we had an ordering change in v2 rollout to prefer higher-capacity pools.
Matt: that ordering + header normalization = silent migration. we need to avoid any implicit semantics change.
Jon: immediate mitigation — revert the normalization in proxy and add a strict-mode flag that requires exact-match. also surface "coerced version" as a console telemetry signal.
Anna: agree. also quota accounting could double-charge if token quota maps differ between v1 and v2 routes.
Tara: good catch. telemetry shows a small number of double-dip billing events — likely because route changed mid-request for streaming sessions.
Matt: streaming sessions are sticky by session-id, but header coercion happened before session-binding. fix order-of-ops: bind session first, then compute header match.
Jon: proposed steps: 1) rollback header normalization in edge proxy (hotfix), 2) add strict-match toggle on console (default off for legacy), 3) add a new telemetry field `version_match_reason` with values ["exact","normalized","fallback"], 4) run a 24h shadow test with strict-match on 10% tenants.
Anna: for the console UX — we should show coerced count per-tenant and let tenant owners opt-in to strict mode with a warning and graceful fallback window.
Tara: logging: include the original header value in traces (PII safe?) — we should redact if it contains customer tokens. probably fine to keep just the header string.
Matt: also add a short-run alert to paging if coerced routing > 0.5% of requests for a tenant for >10m.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: proxy-hotfix-v0.9.3 -> edge-canary (1 node). ETA 12m.
Jon: thanks. I'll open a small docs blurb for the console so tenant ops see the toggle and the telemetry meaning.
Anna: assign follow-ups: @matt do the telemetry field and billing audit, @tara do router ordering rollback if needed, @jon do proxy hotfix and docs. respond here when done.
Matt: on it. starting a quick audit now.
Tara: will watch the canary and check sticky binding order.
Jon: canary looks healthy after the hotfix. no coerced routes in the last 6m. leaving thread open for final billing audit.
Matt: preliminary audit shows ~120 requests that were double-accounted (small $ delta). will reconcile and prepare customer communications if needed.
Anna: thanks team. follow up in #eng-platform tomorrow with postmortem notes and any console copy for the toggle. :thumbsup:
